added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(c_{\mathrm{reg}}>0\), there is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(c_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and the fixed class constants and uniform over the exponent window \(K\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Reg}(c_{\mathrm{reg}})}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/4}.
\]
This is attained by the same total global-bandwidth estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) as in the isolated and pervasive conclusions; it uses neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(c_{\mathrm{reg}}>0\), put \(\rho_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\), and take \(n\) sufficiently large that \(0<\rho_n<h_0\) and the smallest element of \(H_n\) is below \(\rho_n\).  The dyadic form of \(H_n\) then supplies \(h_\rho\in H_n\) such that
\[
 \rho_n\leq h_\rho<2\rho_n. \tag{R1}
\]
Let \(P\in\mathrm{Reg}(c_{\mathrm{reg}})\).  By the definition of this class, there is some \(\kappa_P\in K\) such that \(P\in\mathrm{Base}_{\kappa_P}\), and
\[
 a_P(x,h)\geq c_{\mathrm{reg}}h^2
 \quad\text{for every }x\in B\text{ and }0<h\leq h_0. \tag{R2}
\]
The packing argument on the unit-length segment \(B\) used in \((\mathrm{E11})\) depends on neither the law nor the severity threshold, and therefore
\[
 1\vee J_P(h,u)\leq 2/h
 \quad\text{for every }0<h\leq h_0\text{ and }u\geq0. \tag{R3}
\]
Combining \((\mathrm{R1})\)--\((\mathrm{R3})\), for every \(x\in B\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &Lh_\rho+\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee
 J_P(h_\rho,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h_\rho)\})\}\right)}
 {n a_P(x,h_\rho)}}\\
 &\qquad\leq 2L\rho_n+
 \frac{C\sigma}{\sqrt{c_{\mathrm{reg}}}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(e/h_\rho)}{nh_\rho^2}}\\
 &\qquad\leq C\rho_n. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{R4}
\]
For the last step, \(h_\rho\geq\rho_n\) implies \(\log(e/h_\rho)\leq C\log(en)\), while \(n\rho_n^4=\log n\).  The constant in the oracle theorem is uniform over \(\kappa_P\in K\), so the theorem applies to every member of the displayed union with the same \(C\).  Its remainder satisfies \(\log^2(en)/n=o(\rho_n)\).  Evaluating its bandwidth infimum at \(h_\rho\), taking the supremum over \(x\), and then over \(P\in\mathrm{Reg}(c_{\mathrm{reg}})\), proves the asserted risk bound.  Finally, the explicit construction of \(\widehat\tau_n\) contains neither \(\kappa_P\), \(c_{\mathrm{reg}}\), nor a class label.  Hence this is the identical estimator used for both depleted endpoint bounds.

proposed.name: Regular side-mass design class
proposed.construction:
For (c_{mathrm{reg}}>0), define
\[
 mathrm{Reg}(c_{mathrm{reg}})=
 \left\{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa:
 \inf_{\substack{x\in B\\0<h\leq h_0}}
 \frac{a_P(x,h)}{h^2}\geq c_{\mathrm{reg}}\right\}.
\]

prose_updates.tldr: One explicit split-sample global-bandwidth severity-net estimator, using neither \(\kappa\) nor a regime label, attains the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and the classical regular-design rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The regular exponent is not claimed as new; the contribution is its simultaneous attainment by the same procedure together with the two depleted-design rates.

project_justification.gap: Boundary regression with regular or vanishing one-sided mass needs one measurable causal-trace estimator whose stochastic index set reflects thin-site multiplicity without first knowing the exponent or choosing a profile regime.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is a global-bandwidth empirical severity-net oracle over the declared bivariate side-mass classes, together with a direct evaluation on regular, isolated, and pervasive designs. The regular \(1/4\) exponent is classical; the cross-regime attainment is the new role of that corollary.
project_justification.fill: Lower-mass bands and ordered greedy anchors control the conditional maximum by \(1\vee J_P\). Evaluating the proved oracle at the isolated, pervasive, and regular balances yields all three rates for the identical total estimator, with no preliminary regime selection and no use of \(\kappa\) in its construction.

prose_updates.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies univariate regularly varying designs and pointwise minimax behavior; Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise adaptation over smoothness in an inhomogeneous univariate design, and its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation whereas the present \(L\) is fixed; Gaiffas (2009) uses spatially normalized loss for univariate designs with finitely many density zeros. Their dimensions, targets, and losses differ, so none of those classes includes the present class or is included by it. Product embeddings may support lower submodels, but they do not transfer an upper theorem. For a continuous score density bounded below by \(\underline f>0\) on the \(h_0\)-neighborhood of \(B\), each one-sided half-ball has area \(\pi h^2/2\), and hence \(a_P(x,h)\geq(\pi\underline f/2)h^2\), including the endpoints of the declared segment. Thus the positive-density boundary design of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu overlaps the present \(\mathrm{Reg}(c_{\mathrm{reg}})\) class only after matching the conditional \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian tail, trace envelope, Lipschitz, and frozen base-mass constants. In particular, for each declared \(\kappa>2\), the regular lower bound implies \(q_t(x,h)\geq c_mh^\kappa\) when \(c_m\leq c_{\mathrm{reg}}h_0^{2-\kappa}\). Their full class has different tail and smoothness conditions, and its upper theorem does not transfer to the present vanishing-density laws. A converse transfers only on an exact common subclass, under the same loss and an unrestricted estimator class. The regular rate is classical; only simultaneous attainment by the same severity-net estimator together with the isolated and pervasive rates is claimed here.
prose_updates.interpretation: A regular design has two-dimensional one-sided ball mass of order \(h^2\), so the universal segment packing bound contributes the familiar supremum logarithm and the oracle balance is \(h+\sqrt{\log(1/h)/(nh^2)}\), giving \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\). Under isolated thinning, the severity-dependent packing envelope removes that logarithm at the worst site; under pervasive thinning, the segment-wide packing logarithm remains. Because the same first-half severity net and one selected global bandwidth implement every case, these are genuine same-procedure conclusions rather than an oracle switch among estimators.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved oracle is evaluated for one explicit, total estimator on three law-defined regimes: regular side mass, isolated thinning, and pervasive thinning. The resulting upper rates are \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), respectively, and the estimator uses neither the exponent nor a regime label. The regular exponent is a classical benchmark, not a new minimax claim. Comparator transfer is asserted only on an exact common subclass with matching assumptions, loss, and estimator quantifiers. No arbitrary-profile, pointwise-bandwidth, local-oracle, or arbitrary-pattern simultaneous-band claim is made.
